y digits past the second are kept, so `parseNear(formatNear(x)) === x` holds for every input, as the README requires. The one place this departs from a literal "exactly two decimal places" reading is amounts with more than two significant decimals, such as 1 yoctoNEAR, which print with up to 24 places. I chose the round-trip rule because the README states it as a hard invariant.

I did not run extra edge-case checks because the shell command needed approval. The edge cases (0, 1 yocto, values at the `10^30` bound) follow from the code by reading it, but they are unverified by execution.
